citeAs: Suzgun, M., Scales, N., Schärli, N., Gehrmann, S., Tay, Y., Chung, H. W., Chowdhery, A., Le, Q. V., Chi, E. H., Zhou, D., & Wei, J. (2022). Challenging BIG-Bench tasks and whether chain-of-thought can solve them. arXiv:2210.09261.
creator: Mirac Suzgun, Nathan Scales, Nathanael Schärli, Sebastian Gehrmann, Yi Tay, Hyung Won Chung, Aakanksha Chowdhery, Quoc V. Le, Ed H. Chi, Denny Zhou, Jason Wei (Google Research, Stanford University)
description: BIG-Bench Hard (BBH) is a curated subset of 23 particularly challenging BIG-Bench tasks (27 subtasks) for which no prior language model result outperformed the average human-rater score. The benchmark contains 6,511 evaluation examples spanning tasks requiring multi-step reasoning, algorithmic reasoning, and natural language understanding, and is designed to evaluate chain-of-thought prompting in large language models.
name: BIG-Bench Hard (BBH)
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The authors manually composed three chain-of-thought exemplars for each of the 23 tasks in BBH. All prompts include a task description, few-shot chain-of-thought examples with "let's think step-by-step" prepended to CoT annotations, and answer options. The ground-truth labels come from the original BIG-Bench tasks.
rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that human-rater performance scores are not fully representative of human performance, as the human evaluation took almost a year during which task formatting and content changed multiple times, raters were allocated only a few hours per day, and in some cases task descriptions were hard to follow. Some tasks require factual and general knowledge about Western society (e.g., Movie Recommendation, Ruin Names), which may introduce cultural bias. The paper explicitly cautions that surpassing average human-rater performance should not be confused with true language understanding or reasoning.
rai:dataCollection: BBH was constructed by filtering the BIG-Bench benchmark using a series of criteria: tasks with more than three subtasks were removed; tasks with fewer than 103 examples were removed; tasks without human-rater baselines were removed; tasks not using multiple-choice or exact match evaluation were removed; tasks where the best reported model already beat the average human-rater were removed; and tasks deemed extremely difficult or outside scope (requiring domain-specific knowledge or not solvable within 20 minutes) were removed. The remaining 23 tasks form BBH.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw source data is the BIG-Bench benchmark (Srivastava et al., 2022), a diverse evaluation suite with over 200 text-based tasks covering traditional NLP, mathematics, commonsense reasoning, and question-answering, contributed by a large collaborative effort.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataLimitations: BBH excludes 13 tasks deemed extremely difficult (e.g., Checkmate in One, Real or Fake Text, Moral Permissibility) that require domain-specific knowledge or are not practically solvable within twenty minutes. Human-rater baselines are not fully representative of human performance due to inconsistencies in the BIG-Bench evaluation process. The benchmark uses only multiple-choice or exact-match evaluation metrics, which may not capture all aspects of model capability. Some tasks require knowledge specific to Western culture.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Tasks were filtered from BIG-Bench using the following sequential criteria: (1) tasks with more than three subtasks removed; (2) tasks with fewer than 103 examples removed; (3) tasks without human-rater baselines removed; (4) tasks not using multiple-choice or exact match evaluation removed; (5) tasks where the best reported model beat the average human-rater removed; (6) extremely difficult tasks outside scope removed. For all but three tasks (Causal Judgement, Penguins in a Table, Snarks), a random subset of 250 evaluation examples was taken; for those three tasks all available test examples were used.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper explicitly states that surpassing average human-rater performance on a set of challenging tasks should not be confused with true language understanding or reasoning. The benchmark is intended to facilitate further research on the capabilities and limitations of large language models. The paper also notes that tasks involving moral judgment (e.g., Moral Permissibility) were excluded to avoid delegating agency to models about moral judgment scenarios.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating the capabilities of large language models on challenging reasoning tasks; studying the effect of chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting on model performance; investigating emergent task performance as a function of model scale; benchmarking few-shot prompting approaches on tasks requiring multi-step reasoning.

null_reasons.license: No license is explicitly stated in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:annotationsPerItem: BBH reuses BIG-Bench tasks; no new per-item annotation count is described for BBH itself.
null_reasons.rai:annotatorDemographics: No demographics of annotators are described for BBH; the paper only notes that BIG-Bench human raters were allocated a few hours per day but provides no demographic details.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: No inter-annotator agreement or annotation quality analysis is reported for BBH.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: No annotation platform is mentioned for BBH; the CoT exemplars were written by the paper's authors directly.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: No discussion of missing data handling in the BBH dataset construction.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: No specific timeframe for data collection is stated for BBH; the paper was submitted October 2022.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation protocol is described; BBH is a curated subset of existing tasks.
null_reasons.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: No post-collection data manipulation (augmentation, balancing, resampling) is described for the BBH dataset itself.
null_reasons.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: No versioning or maintenance plan is described in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:machineAnnotationTools: No machine annotation tools were used in constructing BBH; it is a filtered subset of BIG-Bench with manually written CoT prompts.
null_reasons.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: BBH contains reasoning and NLP tasks with no personal or sensitive information about individuals.
